_: The operating systems MXFS is released for, in development for, or planned for. Read and written by tools/platforms.py. status: released = a release claims it, so every release must pass its build_check and record a verification of that exact version (scripts/release.sh refuses to publish otherwise); development = worked on, never claimed; planned = not started. A defect's `platform` field (tools/defects.py) names one of these keys, or `any`.

pve9.name: Proxmox VE 9 (kernels 6.17 and 7.0)
pve9.verify_env: pve9-1 192.168.120.194, pve9-2 192.168.120.138 (libvirt on the rig host), shared QNAP LUN over in-guest iSCSI
pve9.verify_tests: install both .debs from the built packages; DKMS builds on every installed PVE kernel; for EACH claimed kernel (pinned with proxmox-boot-tool, rebooted into): mount with no options on both nodes; cross-node checksums; create/remote-delete counts; chk_mxfs clean; peer= with multicast blocked; peers=; pvesm add/status/remove holds one mount; O_DIRECT read on a stable-writes device; reboot on that kernel, module auto-loaded, remount, earlier data intact (tests/packaged_round.sh pve with KERNEL=)

ubuntu2404.name: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (GA kernel 6.8)
kernels: 6.8.0-101-generic (the 24.04 GA kernel; the HWE kernels 6.11+ are not verified)
ubuntu2404.verify_env: two Ubuntu 24.04 KVM guests on the rig host (test3/test4, 6.8.0-101-generic) sharing the QNAP LUN over in-guest iSCSI, for the packaged install; the rig (test1..test32) for the suite
ubuntu2404.verify_tests: the full 2/tcp suite (run.sh 2 tcp) on the rig; install the .deb from the built packages with a DKMS build and a module loaded from updates/dkms; mount with no options on both nodes; cross-node checksums; create/remote-delete counts; chk_mxfs clean; peer= with multicast blocked; reboot, module auto-loaded, remount, earlier data intact
ubuntu2404.notes: The development rig's platform. Reboots of the rig guests took ~3 min because their iSCSI node records for the SCST target on the rig host (iqn.2026-05.local.mxfs:shared, 192.168.120.1/.2) were set to log in at boot and waited out their timeouts whenever that target was down (systemd-analyze blame: open-iscsi 2 min); set to manual on test1-test4 in 0.89.84, a reboot takes ~30 s. scripts/mpath_up.sh sets them back to automatic when it brings that rig up.

rhel9.name: RHEL / AlmaLinux / Rocky 9.8
kernels: 5.14.0-687.49.1.el9_8 (9.8; earlier minors carry fewer backports and are not verified)
rhel9.verify_env: two AlmaLinux 9.8 QEMU guests on the rig host (alma9-1 192.168.120.100, alma9-2 192.168.120.157; osimager spec alma-9.7 updated to 9.8), kernel 5.14.0-687.49.1.el9_8, firewalld active, SELinux enforcing, shared QNAP LUN over in-guest iSCSI. AlmaLinux and Rocky rebuild Red Hat's kernel for each minor release; runtime runs on AlmaLinux, build checks on AlmaLinux and Rocky.
rhel9.verify_tests: install the .rpm from the built packages with a DKMS build and the module loaded from /lib/modules/<krel>/extra; firewalld with only 7600/tcp 7601/udp 7603/udp opened; mount with no options on both nodes; cross-node checksums; create/remote-delete counts; chk_mxfs clean; peer= with multicast dropped; reboot, module auto-loaded, remount, earlier data intact; SELinux enforcing: mount, cross-node writes, no AVC denials; hung-node freeze (tests/tcp_peer_freeze_death.sh, PREP=alma): death declared, fence certified, replay, survivor writing
rhel9.notes: Ported in 0.89.82: kernel APIs are probed at build time (pal/linux/kcompat_probe.sh), since RHEL 9 reports 5.14 for every minor release while carrying backports, so each minor is a different build. The claim is 9.8 only. Runtime runs on AlmaLinux 9.8 (alma9-1/alma9-2), which rebuilds Red Hat's kernel: the lab has no Red Hat subscription, so the RHEL VMs (rhel9-1/rhel9-2) stay on 9.2 and are the pair for a 9.2 claim. Guests on QEMU need x86-64-v2 (-cpu host).

rhel10.name: RHEL / AlmaLinux / Rocky 10
rhel10.notes: RHEL 10 runs 6.12 plus Red Hat backports: nearer the tree than RHEL 9's 5.14, so it is expected to be cheaper than RHEL 9. Build with scripts/rhel_kbuild_check.sh -i almalinux:10; osimager has rhel-10.x and alma-10.x specs. AlmaLinux and Rocky rebuild the same kernel: runtime on RHEL, build checks on all three.

rhel8.name: RHEL / AlmaLinux / Rocky 8
rhel8.notes: Ordered after RHEL 10 and Debian 12 by user decision, despite its large installed base: 4.18 is the widest API gap of the Linux targets (docs/future.md), and RHEL 8 is in its maintenance phase, so supporting it is a port in its own right, not a build check.

freebsd14.name: FreeBSD 14
freebsd14.notes: A port, not a build target: MXFS is a fork of Linux XFS built as a Linux kernel module. The DLM layer sits behind the platform abstraction (pal/) and carries over; the filesystem needs a new FreeBSD VFS frontend and buffer cache integration (docs/future.md).

ubuntu2604.name: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
ubuntu2604.notes: The current Ubuntu LTS. Its kernel is close to the upstream tree MXFS forks, so the port should be a build check and a packaged round.

debian13.name: Debian 13
debian13.notes: Proxmox VE 9 is built on it, with Proxmox's own newer kernel. Plain Debian runs 6.12, which is also the base of RHEL 10 and SLES 16, so the 6.12 build serves all three.

sles16.name: SUSE Linux Enterprise Server 16
sles16.notes: Rides on the 6.12 build that Debian 13 and RHEL 10 need. Packaging differs: SUSE ships out-of-tree modules as KMPs, not DKMS. SUSE already supports OCFS2 in its HA extension. SLES 15 (6.4 with SUSE backports) is a separate port and is not planned.

macos26.name: macOS 26 Tahoe
packages: signed and notarized kext in a .pkg (universal arm64 + x86_64)
macos26.notes: A kernel extension (user decision, 2026-09-24): the XFS layer and DLM run in XNU behind a new pal/ implementation. Requirements: Apple must grant the kext-signing entitlement on request (a Developer ID alone does not sign kexts); notarization; user approval in System Settings on first load; on Apple Silicon, every Mac must first be set to Reduced Security in Recovery with kernel extensions from identified developers allowed, a one-time documented install step (ATTO's customers do the same). Universal binary: macOS 26 is the last release for Intel Macs. Storage: macOS has no built-in iSCSI initiator; either sit on ATTO's or globalSAN's initiator, where fencing depends on SCSI persistent reservations passing through their stack, or ship one. Apple's Xsan (StorNext-compatible) is the incumbent shared-SAN filesystem on the Mac.

debian12.name: Debian 12
debian12.notes: Large installed base (Debian's previous stable, LTS to mid-2028). 6.1 is below the 6.8 floor MXFS builds on today, so it is a port (VFS/block API shims for 6.1), smaller than RHEL 8's. The release packages are already built in a debian:bookworm container, so the userspace tools run there.

debian11.name: Debian 11
debian11.verify_env: the user's HP server running Debian 11
debian11.notes: Added at the user's request for an HP server running Debian 11 (bullseye, LTS to mid-2026, ELTS after). 5.10 is below both the 6.8 floor MXFS builds on today and Debian 12's 6.1, so it is a port that extends the 6.1 shims further back. The release packages are built in a debian:bookworm container (glibc 2.36); bullseye has glibc 2.31, so the userspace tools need a bullseye build before they run there.

raspios11.name: Raspberry Pi OS 11
raspios11.verify_env: the user's Raspberry Pi running Raspberry Pi OS 11 (bullseye)
raspios11.notes: Added at the user's request for a Raspberry Pi running Raspberry Pi OS 11 (Debian 11 bullseye base). A new architecture as well as a new kernel: every package MXFS builds today is amd64, and the module has never been compiled for ARM. It needs an arm64 (or, on a 32-bit install, armhf) .deb with the tools built in a bullseye container, and a DKMS build against raspberrypi-kernel-headers, the Foundation's own kernel rather than Debian's. The kernel API port is the Debian 11 one; the architecture work is separate, and a 32-bit armhf userland also needs every 64-bit on-disk and DLM quantity checked for 32-bit long and size_t. Check uname -m on the Pi before choosing arm64 or armhf.
